name: Digital wavetable pad with series filter, chorus, echo, space
goal: Craft a digital ambient pad: WT engine with long env→WT position, long amp attack/release, classic unison (~3 voices, wide stereo, ~1–2% detune) layered with a pure sine WT, series LP24→HP12 both opened by the morph env (band-pass-like), velocity amp mod, then Juno-style chorus → tape/ping-pong echo → long wet reverb (chorus also on the reverb path).

source.title: Arturia Pigments: Creating A Digital Pad

prerequisites: Dual-engine wavetable synth, dual filters routable in series, chorus, delay, reverb, macros/sends
constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided captions; do not invent UI or settings.
Original synthesis only — map brand UI (Serum/Vital/Pigments/Phase Plant/etc.) to portable osc/filter/FX roles for a browser or generic hybrid synth; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Prefer transferable signal-flow and motion relationships over vendor-specific preset names.
If reverb is on a parallel aux, duplicate chorus onto the aux if you want chorused space.
Use stock/original wavetables; ignore preset-pack names from the video.

steps.action: Engine1 wavetable (additive/gentle digital): set mid position; env2 → WT position with long attack, slow decay, high sustain, long release.
Amp/VCA env: attack ~2.8s, full sustain, release ~5s+.
Engine2: basic sine WT, unison ~3 / stereo 100% / ~1% detune; blend under the bright digital engine for weight.
Series filters: LP24 (cutoff low hundreds Hz, light resonance, key follow ~0.4) then HP12 (~50 Hz); both cutoffs also from env2 so morph opens LP while HP removes some sine weight over time.

Insert Juno-like chorus (slow rate ~0.25 Hz, depth a few ms, phase ~180°); send to aux: chorus copy → tape/ping-pong echo (e.g. 1/4, ~50% wet, feedback ~0.35) → 100% wet long reverb (long predelay/decay, damping, HP/LP).

verification: WT position moves on a long envelope
Sine layer adds weight under digital WT
Filters in series behave like a controllable band
Chorus present on the reverberated path if using parallel reverb
